title: Lobbying Disclosure (LDA.gov API)
agency: Secretary of the Senate (Office of Public Records) and Clerk of the House
questions: how much did a company spend on lobbying each year
lobbying on an issue such as tax or health by a company

key_only: 120 requests a minute instead of 15 (large downloads finish 8 times faster)

manual.how: Open each JSON link in INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser (no key needed; 25 filings per page, at most 15 pages a minute) and save it under the given name; or use the search forms at https://lda.gov/filings/public/filing/search/ (LD-1/LD-2) and https://lda.gov/filings/public/contribution/search/ (LD-203) and download the result list, then upload the files.

cache.why: Filings and amendments post continuously; data/ is reused within a run.

redistribution.why: The Lobbying Disclosure Act requires the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House to make filings public; the LDA.gov terms set no controls on end use but require the access date, the Office of Public Records disclaimer, and no modified or misrepresented content cited as LDA.gov.

notices: Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after the data have been retrieved from LDA.gov.
citation: U.S. Senate Office of Public Records, Lobbying Disclosure Act database (LDA.gov API), {dataset}, data accessed {retrieved_long}.

audit_hooks.why: LDA.gov terms of service: users must state that the Senate Office of Public Records cannot vouch for data or analyses after retrieval

clarify: Spending of the client itself (in-house expenses) or also outside firms' income from that client? Adding both double counts when the client's own report includes payments to firms.
Original reports or amended ones? Default: the latest amendment replaces the original for the same registrant, client and period.
